papers.title_en: High-Fidelity 4D Hand-Object Capture via Multi-View Spatiotemporal Tracking and Physics-Aware Gaussians
papers.authors: Bo Peng, Xu Chen, Yi Gu, Hidenobu Matsuki, Mingsong Dou, Jingjing Shen, Deying Kong, Juyong Zhang, Zhengyang Shen
papers.evidence: 使用物理感知高斯重建4D手物交互
papers.tldr: 当前4D手物交互重建依赖预扫描模板和物理标记，且对初始位姿估计高度敏感，尤其在严重遮挡下。本文提出多视图时空跟踪与物理感知高斯方法，通过多视图Transformer初始化位姿与几何，并利用物理感知高斯优化框架进行精炼，融入四面体约束、碰撞精炼和外观分解。在公开基准和大规模内部数据集上实现鲁棒、无伪影的重建，为自动化4D资产生成提供高效基础。
papers.abstract_en: The growing demand for high-fidelity 4D hand-object interaction (HOI) data in embodied AI and spatial computing is currently bottlenecked by the reliance on pre-scanned object templates and physical markers. While recent methods have demonstrated promising results in reconstructing 4D hand-object interaction from videos, they are highly sensitive to initial estimates of hand and object poses. Yet, estimating these poses from images is challenging, in particular under severe occlusion which is inherent in hand-object interaction scenarios. We propose a novel system for the robust and accurate reconstruction of hands and objects from synchronized and calibrated multi-view videos without requiring any templates or markers. Our system consists of two main components with key innovations: (1) a multi-view feed-forward transformer model that aggregates cross-view geometry and temporal cues to provide a reliable, metric-consistent initialization for both poses and dense object geometry, and (2) a hand-object physics-aware Gaussian-based optimization framework to refine the initial estimates, integrating tetrahedral constraints, collision refinement, and appearance decomposition to produce physically plausible and visually accurate reconstruction. Validated on public benchmarks and an extensive internal dataset, our pipeline achieves highly robust, artifact-free reconstruction, providing an efficient foundation for automated 4D asset generation. Our project page are available at https://zyshen021.github.io/HOSTPG/.

papers.title_en: AIGS-Net: Compact Illumination Field Modeling via 2D Gaussian Splatting for Fast Low-Light Image Enhancement
papers.authors: Yuhan Chen, Kunyang Huang, Fuchen Li, Zhuohan Qin, Guofa Li, Wenbo Chu, Keqiang Li
papers.evidence: 使用2D高斯溅射进行低光图像增强中的自适应光照场建模
papers.tldr: 现有低光图像增强方法常受制于光照场建模的表征能力与计算开销之间的瓶颈。AIGS-Net提出自适应二维高斯散斑光照场，利用输入相对亮度统计动态调节高斯基透明度，通过有序alpha合成实现空间变化光照补偿。同时引入零参数非线性多尺度上下文编码模块提取低频结构与局部对比度，并集成噪声掩码估计、锁定单通道Gamma映射、跨通道一致性正则化与目标颜色对齐约束以抑制噪声和偏色。在LOL与LSRW基准上，模型仅需约40个可学习参数，即取得细节恢复和色彩保真度的提升，实现增强质量与极端推理效率的有效平衡。
papers.abstract_en: Existing low-light image enhancement methods often face a bottleneck between the representation capacity of illumination-field modeling and computational complexity. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Adaptive Illumination Gaussian Splatting Network (AIGS-Net), an ultra-lightweight architecture for fast low-light enhancement. Unlike conventional static priors, AIGS-Net constructs an input-adaptive 2D Gaussian Splatting illumination field. The opacity of Gaussian basis functions is dynamically modulated by relative luminance statistics of the input image, and spatially varying illumination compensation is rendered through ordered alpha compositing. To guide adaptive illumination compensation efficiently, a zero-parameter nonlinear multiscale contextual encoding module is introduced to extract low-frequency structures and local contrast cues without additional convolutional weights. To suppress noise amplification and sensor-induced color bias, AIGS-Net integrates noise-mask estimation, locked single-channel Gamma mapping, cross-channel consistency regularization, and target color-alignment constraints. Experiments on LOL and LSRW benchmarks show that AIGS-Net improves detail recovery and color fidelity while requiring only approximately 40 learnable parameters, achieving an effective trade-off between enhancement quality and extreme inference efficiency.

papers.title_en: LIT-GS: LiDAR-Inertial-Thermal Gaussian Splatting for Illumination-Robust Mapping
papers.authors: Shikuan Shi, Chunran Zheng, Jiaming Xu, Tianyong Ye, Tao Yu, Yukang Cui
papers.evidence: 在高斯泼溅映射框架中联合优化相机位姿
papers.tldr: 现有激光雷达-惯性-视觉高斯泼溅方法依赖RGB光度线索，在光照变化或弱纹理场景易失效。LIT-GS引入热成像与激光雷达平面几何约束，通过跨模态锚点关联与平面正则化优化，联合改善位姿与结构。实验表明，在低光等挑战条件下几何精度与渲染质量显著超越现有基线，为光照鲁棒三维建图提供了新途径。
papers.abstract_en: Gaussian Splatting has enabled real-time neural rendering, yet existing LiDAR-inertial-visual (LIV) Gaussian mapping pipelines remain fragile under illumination changes and texture-deficient scenes due to their reliance on RGB photometric cues. We present LIT-GS, a LiDAR-inertial-thermal Gaussian Splatting framework that injects LiDAR-derived plane geometry as an explicit constraint in both pose/structure refinement and Gaussian optimization. Specifically, we exploit LIV visual map points as confidence-aware cross-modal anchors to establish reliable thermal-LiDAR associations, and incorporate weighted LiDAR point-to-plane residuals into bundle adjustment to jointly refine camera poses and 3D points under weak thermal supervision. Building on the refined structure, we further introduce a LiDAR-plane-regularized differentiable splatting objective that constrains rendered 3D points to align with locally observed planes, mitigating surface thickening and structural drift in low-contrast thermal imagery. Experiments on proprietary sequences and public datasets demonstrate that LIT-GS consistently improves geometric accuracy and rendering quality over state-of-the-art LIV-based Gaussian Splatting baselines, particularly in challenging lighting conditions.

papers.title_en: VisDom: Sparse Novel View Synthesis with Visible Domain Constraint
papers.authors: Mariia Gladkova*, Tarun Yenamandra*, Edmond Boyer, Robert Maier, Tony Tung, Daniel Cremers
papers.evidence: 为3D高斯泼溅新视角合成引入多视图可见性约束
papers.tldr: 稀疏新视图合成因输入视图稀少，NeRF与GS方法易过拟合产生漂浮伪影，轮廓正则化不足以约束几何。VisDom引入无学习几何约束，通过要求体素被至少K个视图可见来过滤视觉外壳，提供强空间先验。集成到NeRF与GS管线后，仅用四张图像即可实现高质量重建，性能媲美GaussianObject且训练成本降低22倍。该方法仅需轮廓、领域无关，可作为现有方法的简单增强。
papers.abstract_en: Sparse novel view synthesis (NVS) remains challenging due to the ambiguity of recovering 3D geometry from few input views. While NeRF- and Gaussian Splatting (GS)-based methods perform well with dense supervision, they often overfit in sparse settings, producing floating artifacts and inconsistent geometry. Silhouette consistency is commonly used as a regularizer, but it remains insufficient, as silhouette-consistent regions can extend beyond the true object geometry. We introduce VisDom, a learning-free geometric constraint that augments classical carving-based visual hull reconstruction by enforcing a minimum multi-view visibility requirement. Specifically, we define a visible domain as the subset of 3D space observed by at least $K$ views and use it as an additional filtering criterion on top of standard silhouette-based reconstruction. This provides a stronger spatial prior in sparse-view settings. We integrate VisDom into both implicit (NeRF) and explicit (GS) pipelines by restricting volumetric sampling and guiding Gaussian placement during optimization. Experiments on three challenging datasets show consistent improvements in sparse-view NVS, enabling high-quality object-centric reconstruction from as few as four input images. Our method is domain-agnostic, requires only silhouettes, and introduces no learned parameters, making it a simple complement to existing approaches. Applying VisDom on top of GaussianObject further improves performance on Omni3D and MipNeRF360, while matching or surpassing it at 22 $\times$ lower training cost.
